From the School

A Triumphant
Close to the Session

"All praise is due to Almighty Allāh — Lord of all worlds, Master of all affairs, and the sole Author of every success we celebrate. We are profoundly grateful for His mercy, which carried us through this entire session: every lesson taught, every challenge overcome, and every student who arrived back a little wiser, a little stronger, and a little more ready for what lies ahead."

The third term is always a special one. It carries the weight of a full year's effort and the promise of a well-deserved rest. But before the rest comes the finish — and our students finished this session with unmistakable energy and resolve.

This term, Taqwa High School did not merely conclude a school year. We crowned it. With competitions won on stages beyond our walls, celebrations that reminded us who we are as a community, and academic results that reflect the relentless investment of our teachers, students, and parents, this final term was a statement — the kind that sets up an even more powerful 2026/2027 session.

To every parent who trusted us with your child this year: thank you. This newsletter is a small window into the world you helped us build together.

3rd
Term — Session Complete
The 2025/2026 academic session draws to a close — and what a journey it has been. Every arm of the school rose to meet its challenges with maturity and purpose.

Academics & Assessment

The Numbers That Tell
the Real Story

End-of-session results are always a moment of reckoning — but also of celebration. This term, we put every student through a rigorous end-of-term examination designed not just to test recall, but to assess genuine understanding, application, and depth. The outcomes reaffirm what our staff have worked all year to build.

Our Holistic Performance Index is not a number to be read in isolation — it is a composite of who our students are: intellectually capable, morally grounded, and spiritually rooted. Across all year groups, this final term’s results reflect individual effort as much as the investment our teachers poured into every classroom, every day. That is the Taqwa model.

Results have been published on the school portal, and direct links have been sent to each parent's registered email address — so accessing your child's report has never been easier.

Check your registered email for a direct link to your child's end-of-session report.

For any access issues, please contact the school office directly and we will assist you promptly.

Term Highlights

Remarkable Moments
in Pictures

01
External Competition

MSSN Lagos Intellectual Competitions 2026 — Junior Quiz

They sent one student. She came back with a cheque for ₦100,000 and the school's name ringing in the halls of the MSSN Lagos Intellectual Competitions 2026. Aisha Akingbolu represented Taqwa High School in the Junior Quiz Category — competing against schools from across Lagos State in a contest of intellect, speed, and precision — and emerged in 2nd Position, clinching a prize of one hundred thousand naira. This is what Taqwa looks like beyond our walls. We are immensely proud.

02
Language & Literacy

2026 Annual Spelling Bee — The Finals

After weeks of Preliminary, Qualifying, and Semifinal rounds that steadily narrowed the field, the 2026 Taqwa Spelling Bee culminated in a Finals day that was everything this competition promises — tense, thrilling, and ultimately triumphant. Six students stood on that stage in the Finals across both the Junior and Senior categories. Six students spelled their way through pressure and nerves. And six students reminded us exactly why we run this competition every year: to build vocabulary, yes — but even more, to build character.

03
Community & Fun

Students' Week — Celebrate. Participate. Create Memories.

Four days. One school. Countless memories. Students' Week is our annual celebration of community — a dedicated space in the school calendar where the pressure of academics lifts just enough to let personality, culture, and joy breathe. This year's edition gave students Color Day (each class, one colour, all energy), Jersey Day (sporting pride on full display), Cultural Day (a vibrant tapestry of heritage and identity), and Class Party (the sweet finale — food, games, and the kind of laughter that bonds a class together for life). The Taqwa family showed out, and it was beautiful.

Character & Well-being

The Foundations We Never Move

🤝

Student Conduct

Adab before knowledge — this remains the Taqwa way. As students come back refreshed for a brand new session, we hold the standard high: respect for teachers and peers, honesty in all dealings, and the kind of self-discipline that doesn't need supervision to show up. Good character is not a rule you follow; it is a habit you build, and we are committed to helping every student build it.

👔

Dress Code & Presentation

From day one of resumption, full and correct uniform is non-negotiable. A well-presented student signals a well-ordered mind. Incomplete uniforms will need to be corrected before a student joins class. We are not rigid for the sake of it — we are consistent because consistency builds excellence, and we expect every Taqwa student to embody that excellence from the moment they walk through our gates.

✨

Personal Hygiene

Our standards for personal hygiene — hair properly kept, nails trimmed, general grooming — remain in full effect and will be enforced from the first day back. These habits matter not because we are checking a box, but because the discipline required to maintain them is the same discipline that produces academic excellence. We trust our students to arrive back holding that standard.

Financial Matters

School Fees & Important Notice

Timely payment of school fees enables us to continue delivering the quality of education and environment that our students deserve. We are deeply committed to making this process as clear and convenient as possible for every parent and guardian.

📋 Notice Regarding Term 1 Bills — 2026/2027 Session

We sincerely apologise for the delay in disbursing the fee bills for the upcoming session. This was caused by a technical difficulty in the Accounts Office that affected the timely publication of bills to individual student profiles. We understand that this is inconvenient — parents rightly wish to plan and prepare ahead — and we are truly sorry for any stress this may have caused.

We are pleased to inform you that the issue has been fully resolved, alhamduliLLAH. The Accounts Office will manually send out the bills from tomorrow in sha Allah.

May Allāh continue to ease your affairs, expand your provisions, and reward your patience generously, āmīn.

Payment Guidelines
